analysis.investment_thesis: Craftsman fails my most basic test: Debt/Equity of 1.09 and borrowings that have grown from INR 800 Cr in FY22 to INR 3,311 Cr in FY25 at a company earning only 9.4% ROE is a recipe for value destruction, not creation. A manufacturing business paying INR 217 Cr in finance costs against INR 201 Cr net profit in FY25 is essentially working for its lenders.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 22.8% over 8 years shows genuine commercial execution and customer wins
Diversified across powertrain, aluminium casting, and industrial engineering — some protection from single-segment shocks
OCF has been positive in all 5 observed years, confirming the underlying operations do generate cash
key_risks: D/E of 1.09 violates my absolute limit of 0.3 — debt-funded capex in a cyclical auto-components business is extremely dangerous
ROE of 9.41% and ROCE of 11.7% are below my minimum thresholds — the business is not earning its cost of capital
Net profit fell sharply from INR 337 Cr (FY24) to INR 201 Cr (FY25) — a 40% decline — even as revenue grew, signalling margin compression and rising interest burden
red_flags: Borrowings jumped from INR 1,755 Cr (FY24) to INR 3,311 Cr (FY25) — debt nearly doubled in one year, suggesting a leveraged acquisition
FCF was -INR 706 Cr in FY25 and -INR 115 Cr in FY24 — two consecutive years of deeply negative free cash flow
Finance costs (INR 217 Cr) now nearly equal net profit (INR 201 Cr) — the business is fragile to any rate or demand shock
analysis.detailed_analysis: Craftsman is an operationally capable engineering company building scale aggressively, but it is doing so entirely on borrowed money. I built DMart by never taking on debt I was not completely comfortable with — debt amplifies mistakes and removes options. Here, the debt has more than quadrupled from FY22 to FY25 while ROE sits at 9.4%, which means every rupee of equity is earning less than a fixed deposit. Auto components is an inherently cyclical business, and leveraged cyclicals are the most dangerous category of investment for a long-term holder.
